title: Organize and find your notes
p: Your documents should stay easy to explore as their number grows. Use the document tree to give notes a home, pins and favorites to keep useful pages close, and links and search to find connections.
Click Home in the sidebar or press ⌘ ⌥ Home to see your documents.

ul.li: My documents and Favorites: browse everything or just the pages you have marked.
Sort: choose last opened, last modified, creation time or title. Your choice is remembered.
Grid and list: switch at the top right. Cards show content previews and covers; the list emphasizes document details and dates.
Right-click a card or use its More menu for document actions.

p: Any page can contain other pages. Hover over it in the sidebar and click the plus button to create a child. Parent pages show a folder icon; on hover, the icon gives way to a triangle you can click to expand or collapse the children.

The list above is a child-page list block. It updates automatically as children are added or removed. The path at the top of an open document lets you return to its parent.
Right-click a sidebar entry or click its More button.

td.p: Keep a reference next to the document you are writing.
Create a separate copy you can edit.
Move the page and its children under another document or back to the top level. Search for a destination in the dialog.
Place a shortcut in the sidebar's Pinned section.
Include the document in Home's Favorites tab.
Edit the title in the sidebar. Enter confirms; Esc cancels.
Move the page and its children to Trash.

p: Top-level sidebar documents are ordered by recent modification. Children are shown in sibling order.
Use the batch control beside My documents, or Shift-click a document. Select up to 50 pages, then use the footer to duplicate, move or delete them together. Press Esc to leave batch mode.

callout.p: Visible at the top of the sidebar. Keep a few daily essentials here, such as your weekly plan.
Collected in their own Home tab. Useful for references you want to return to without filling the sidebar.

p: Type @ to see recently opened pages, then type a title to search. Pick a page to insert a link, such as {{doc:writing}}. The link keeps working if the destination is renamed.
The reference area at the end of a document shows incoming and outgoing links. Incoming links include the surrounding text; click one to jump to that mention.
Both example child pages mention this guide, so they appear in its backlinks. You can hide the reference area with its close button and show it again from the document's More menu.

callout.p: The tree answers “Where does this note belong?” Links answer “What is it connected to?” Use both when a note has more than one context.

p: Press ⌘ J or use the search control in the header or on Home. Search matches document titles and body text, prioritizes titles, and shows highlighted snippets.

ul.li: With an empty query, search shows recently visited documents.
Use the arrow keys to select, Enter to open and Esc to close.
You can also search selected text from the formatting toolbar's More menu.

p: Press ⌘ F to find text in the current document. Enter moves to the next match; Shift-Enter moves back. ⌘ ⇧ H opens replacement controls for one match or all matches. Search is case-insensitive.

ul.li: Outline: jump between headings and keep track of the current section. Each document remembers whether its outline is expanded.
Page width: choose the default, wide or full-width layout from the More menu. Wide layouts are useful for tables.
Reading mode: ⌃ ⌥ V makes the view read-only while keeping selection, copying and folding available. ⌃ ⌥ E returns to editing.
Document information: inspect dates, word and character counts, and file size. Words and numbers are counted as words; each CJK character is counted individually.

p: Deleted documents stay in Trash for 30 days before automatic removal. Open Settings › Trash to restore them or delete them permanently.

ul.li: Restore returns a page to its original parent, or to the top level if the parent no longer exists.
Permanent deletion also removes children and cannot be undone.

callout.p: Before permanently deleting something you might need, export a copy or back up your documents.
